name: Daniel
bio:
Daniel, a young Judean noble, was taken to Babylon among the exiles after Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem, and renamed Belteshazzar. Along with three companions, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, he refused to defile himself with the king's food and wine, requesting a ten-day trial on vegetables and water instead; the four emerged healthier than those who ate the royal fare, and excelled all the king's wise men in wisdom and understanding (Daniel 1:1-21).

## 📖 Core Story: Interpreter of Dreams

When Nebuchadnezzar demanded his wise men both describe and interpret a forgotten dream or die, only Daniel could do it, through a vision God gave him: a statue of gold, silver, bronze, iron, and clay, representing a succession of kingdoms, struck down by a stone that grew into a mountain filling the earth — symbolizing God's eternal kingdom replacing all human empires. Nebuchadnezzar fell before Daniel in worship and promoted him to rule over Babylon's wise men (Daniel 2:1-49). Years later, Daniel alone could interpret the king's second dream, of a great tree cut down, warning that Nebuchadnezzar himself would be humbled and live like a beast for seven years until he acknowledged God's sovereignty — a prophecy that came true exactly as Daniel said (Daniel 4:1-37).

## 📖 Core Story: The Fall of Babylon and the Lions' Den

At Belshazzar's drunken feast, when mysterious handwriting appeared on the wall, only Daniel could interpret it: the king's kingdom had been weighed, found wanting, and would be given to the Medes and Persians — a judgment fulfilled that very night (Daniel 5:1-31). Under Darius the Mede, Daniel rose to be one of three chief administrators, provoking jealous rivals to trap him by outlawing prayer to anyone but the king; Daniel kept praying openly anyway, and was thrown into a den of lions. God shut the lions' mouths, and Daniel emerged unharmed the next morning, while his accusers were thrown to the lions in his place (Daniel 6:1-28).

## 📖 Core Story: Visions of the Future

In his later years, Daniel received a series of apocalyptic visions: four beasts representing successive kingdoms followed by the eternal reign of "one like a son of man" (Daniel 7:1-28); a vision of a ram and goat symbolizing Media-Persia and Greece, which troubled him deeply (Daniel 8:1-27); a prayer of confession for Israel's sins after studying Jeremiah's prophecy of seventy years, answered with the revelation of seventy prophetic "weeks" culminating in the Messiah (Daniel 9:1-27); and a final extended vision, delivered by a glorious heavenly messenger, detailing centuries of conflict between northern and southern kingdoms and ending with a promise of resurrection for the righteous dead at the end of days (Daniel 10:1-12:13).
